subject: general
question: Protection of environment and wildlife is mentioned in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 48A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 48A was added to the Indian Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976**.
 
• It is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** under Part IV of the Constitution.
 
• The article directs the State to **protect and improve the environment** and to safeguard forests and wildlife.
 
• It emphasizes the State's responsibility in promoting ecological balance and environmental sustainability.
 
• Article 48A complements Article 51A(g), which highlights the fundamental duty of citizens to protect the environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• DPSPs are non-justiciable guidelines for the State to frame policies aimed at socio-economic welfare.
 
• They are inspired by the Irish Constitution and aim to establish a welfare state.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• Known as the "mini-Constitution," it introduced significant changes, including the addition of Article 48A.
 
• It emphasized environmental protection and aimed to strengthen the Directive Principles.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A(g):**
 
 
• Part of the Fundamental Duties introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act.
 
• It mandates citizens to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.
 
 
 
• **Environment Protection Laws in India:**
 
 
• The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 and the Environment Protection Act, 1986 are key legislations for environmental conservation.
 
• India is also a signatory to several international treaties like the Convention on Biological Diversity and Ramsar Convention.
